title: DoIt rejected-key errors must be registered in get_non_retryable_errors with a reconnect message
answers: DoIt source keeps retrying every sync and never tells user to replace the API key
DoIt 403 invalid token: missing expiration keeps failing
How to stop retrying a warehouse source error that only a new key fixes
body:
Symptom: A DoIt data warehouse source with a rejected API key retries on every sync and fails, and the user is never told to replace the key.
Root cause: products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/doit/source.py:get_non_retryable_errors only matched the 401 text "invalid or revoked access key". DoIt also answers some rejected keys with 403 `invalid token: missing expiration`, which was unclassified and so retried.
Fix pattern: Add the error substring as a key in the get_non_retryable_errors dict, mapped to the shared `bad_key` message ("...create a new key and reconnect."). Keys are substring patterns of the error text.
Constraints: Use only for errors where a retry cannot succeed (bad credentials). The message must keep the word "reconnect"; the test checks for it. New DoIt bad-key texts should reuse the `bad_key` variable.
applies: DoIt warehouse source; the same pattern applies to other sources' get_non_retryable_errors maps.
